newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries dip in London as looming data unnerve.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries dip in London as looming data unnerve.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries dipped lower in thin volume in London on Tuesday with the market focused squarely on impending data, analysts said.

The first quarter employment cost index (ECI), durable goods and consumer confidence data are the first in a string of numbers this week that might give a clue to the Federal Reserve's next move on interest rates.
"We went out strongly in New York but we've faded a bit here. We're not seeing a great deal of volume," said a salesman at a U.S. bank in London.
The long bond was quoted at 93-24 at 0953 GMT, compared with 94-00 in late trade in New York on Monday. The market was closed in Tokyo for a national holiday.

Economists surveyed by Reuters produced a consensus forecast of a 0.9 percent rise in the ECI compared to a 0.8 percent gain in the last quarter. Durable goods were expected to be unchanged after a 1.5 percent rise in February. The April consumer confidence index was seen at 118.4 compared with 118.5 in March.
"The market's fear must be that those numbers are higher, therefore if they come out at consensus given the good bid we had yesterday, they may go higher again," the salesman said.
Dick Howard, senior economist at Julius Baer Investments in London, said it was hard to stray from the market consuses on the ECI.

"We've already had hourly earnings numbers so it does suggest it will come in somewhere between 0.8 and one percent quarter-on-quarter," he said. The report is broken down into a wages and salaries component and a benefits component. Benefits may surprise, Howard said.
The rest of the week includes a report from the National Association of Purchasing Management and the all-important payroll report on Friday.
"It's the sort of week you take it number by number and by Friday we should know what the Fed is going to do," Howard said.
